data.title: Caroli Foods opens solar park at Pitești plant in Romania
data.description: Caroli Foods Group has begun using electricity from a photovoltaic park built next to its packaged meat production plant in Pitești, Argeș county. The project was financed entirely from the company’s own resources. The solar park covers 22,000 square meters and comprises 3,600 monocrystalline photovoltaic panels, each with a capacity of 700 W. Its total installed capacity is 2.52 MW. The annual electricity production is estimated at 2,750 MWh. All the power generated will be used by the Pitești plant, with none fed into the national grid, the company said. By replacing part of the electricity purchased from the grid, the project is expected to avoid approximately 610 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions annually. “Integrating solar energy into the plant’s consumption directly contributes to greater operational efficiency, optimal resource use, and improved predictability of energy costs,” said Adrian Trifan, director of Caroli Foods Group’s Pitești plant. The facility produces more than 200 packaged meat products and ready meals under the Caroli, Sissi, Campofrio, Maestro, and Primo brands. It has an annual production capacity exceeding 30,000 tons and employs approximately 700 people.

data.title: Romanian intelligence service faces backlash after rare response to theory linking it to PSD
data.description: On Tuesday evening, October 20, the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) issued a rare press release rejecting a theory posed by former presidential adviser Ludovic Orban. According to the politician, SRI had brokered a deal that would have the Social Democratic Party (PSD) back sitting president Nicușor Dan for a second mandate during the next presidential elections. Orban explained his theory that the Social Democrats would support Dan in the next presidential election, and in return, they would receive the government. SRI and the Protection and Guard Service (SPP) would have vouched for the Social Democrats, supposedly guaranteeing that the “party was in it for the long haul.” Orban’s statements were made during an interview for the Romanian state TV station TVR. The former presidential adviser also said that SRI chief General Răzvan Ionescu was unknown and that he “runs the SRI on the sly,” according to G4Media . Shortly after the show ended, the SRI posted a rare response on the institution’s Facebook page. “Following the statements made by Mr. Ludovic Orban on public television on October 20, the SRI considers the repeated public dissemination of unfounded accusations, attributing political involvement to the institution without any evidence, to be regrettable and irresponsible,” the agency said. SRI also noted that “the political failure or success of certain political formations or individuals” has been routinely attributed to it without merit. “As regards the interim leadership of the SRI, it is neither secret nor outside the law. And certainly not ‘on the sly.’ The identity of the person serving as interim head is public, and the legality of exercising the position is not a matter of opinion, but is in accordance with the law,” the institution noted. After numerous comments criticizing the service and the response, SRI limited who could comment on the post. The SRI has been under the interim leadership of General Răzvan Ionescu since July 2023. At a press conference on July 30, 2025, president Nicușor Dan said he would appoint heads of the intelligence services “after a discussion with the parties, in the coming weeks.” The president has yet to do so. Reacting to the SRI press release, Liberal MP Alexandru Muraru said on Wednesday, October 21, that the statements made by the agency were “a serious mistake and an unforgivable institutional outburst, almost without precedent.” https://www.facebook.com/muraru2020/posts/pfbid02CSypB4KcuC43hdy42gzyAT32FNbDAdpdy6U6afqdZRWbmEE6TUxV9n7qC2S4sbJhl?locale=ro_RO “Such a reaction risks harming both the person targeted, the credibility of the Service, the reputation of the professionals working at this institution and, above all, public trust in the political neutrality of intelligence services (...) The SRI’s mission is not to engage in public battles with one politician or another, to issue certificates of political responsibility, or to sanction the rhetoric of former or current officials. Its mission is to defend Romania’s national security, the state, and its citizens,” Muraru stated. Cătălin Drulă, an MP from the reformist Save Romania Union (USR), also strongly criticized the SRI’s statement. “The barely veiled threats in the message reveal the anti-democratic reflexes of those running this institution. If our country had a leader who valued freedom of expression, pluralism, and the values of liberal democracy, tomorrow he should fire General Ionescu for this act of intimidation, worthy of illiberal regimes,” Drulă wrote on Facebook .

data.title: Bravva Angels members invest over EUR 220,000 in startups over past three months
data.description: The members of Bravva Angels, a community of investors supporting technology startups from Romania and Central and Eastern Europe, have invested in five companies over the past three months. The list includes Watergenics, Solmag, Rayscape, and EdNeos. The fifth company backed by Bravva Angels members is currently raising a round, but details remain confidential at this stage. The companies have collectively secured more than EUR 220,000 from the over 50 active investors in the Bravva Angels community. In recent months, Bravva has assessed companies in medtech, robotics, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, fintech, e-commerce, and software solutions for managing EV charging stations, it said. Most of the startups are developing SaaS products and operate under B2B, B2B2C, or B2B2B business models. Solmag gives energy suppliers, traders, and distribution system operators real-time visibility into solar power generation directly from inverters, enabling teams to forecast, balance, and respond with less uncertainty and lower risk. The startup, founded by Alex Nicoară and Vlad Ionescu, also offers its own hardware device, which connects and optimizes prosumers’ solar panels and batteries to maximize their energy revenues through a virtual power plant. With the help of the investment, the Solmag team has opened its first hardware manufacturing facility and plans to continue to attract new customers. Watergenics is a Berlin-based startup founded by Romanian entrepreneur Liviu Mantescu. It develops smart sensors and software platforms for real-time water quality monitoring directly at factories and industrial plants. While traditional sensors require water samples to be sent to a laboratory, a process that can take between 12 and 24 hours, Watergenics’ sensor analyzes the chemical composition of water directly in the pipeline and delivers results in less than 10 minutes. Potential applications include mining and lithium extraction, the chemical and petrochemical industries, semiconductor manufacturing, wastewater treatment plants, and water desalination facilities. EdNeos is an AI-powered platform that helps deskless workers develop soft and hard skills by providing continuous voice-based assistance as they carry out their daily tasks. EdNeos founder Veceslav Carbugan initially set out to build an educational assistant for students, designed to improve learning outcomes and retention. Over the years, he identified a strong business use case, with EdNeos able to be integrated directly into the workflows of frontline employees. Today, the platform is used by companies in both Romania and Luxembourg. Rayscape is a European medtech company headquartered in Timișoara that develops artificial intelligence solutions for radiology. Its current portfolio includes software products for analyzing X-rays and chest CT scans. Rayscape’s technologies have been deployed in more than 20 countries and are used by public healthcare providers as well as private medical networks and centers across Europe and other international markets. The funding raised from private investors, alongside financing from investment funds and a grant secured by the Rayscape team, will help expand Rayscape TAP-CT, a product designed to cover the entire thorax-abdomen-pelvis (TAP) CT examination. The risks associated with innovation remain high, but Romanian teams are becoming increasingly effective at defining the problems they solve and developing their business models. “Bravva’s mission is to empower founders to grow their companies by providing not only funding but also expertise. The added value comes from the community, which works alongside founders wherever support is needed. Only by working together can we compete with technology companies in the EU and US. The risks associated with innovation remain high, but Romanian teams are becoming increasingly effective at defining the problems they solve and developing their business models, which investors expect to see validated at a relatively early stage,” Ilinca Păun, founder of Bravva Angels, explained. The team of Bravva speaks with around 15 startups every month, on average. Of these, approximately three are invited to pitch their businesses to the angel investors. The selection criteria include the team’s readiness to scale and raise investment, the size of the market, and the founders’ entrepreneurial stamina. Bravva Angels members are currently assessing 11 new startups for potential investment, following their pitches and in-depth sessions with the teams. Although the community’s portfolio spans multiple sectors, the majority of the companies under consideration are developing SaaS products and operate under B2B, B2B2C, or B2B2B business models. They either target international customers directly or operate in segments of the Romanian market that are large enough to demonstrate traction before moving into their next stage of growth.

Rayscape’s technologies have been deployed in more than 20 countries and are used by public healthcare providers as well as private medical networks and centers across Europe and other international markets. The funding raised from private investors, alongside financing from investment funds and a grant secured by the Rayscape team, will help expand Rayscape TAP-CT, a product designed to cover the entire thorax-abdomen-pelvis (TAP) CT examination. The risks associated with innovation remain high, but Romanian teams are becoming increasingly effective at defining the problems they solve and developing their business models. “Bravva’s mission is to empower founders to grow their companies by providing not only funding but also expertise. The added value comes from the community, which works alongside founders wherever support is needed. Only by working together can we compete with technology companies in the EU and US. The risks associated with innovation remain high, but Romanian teams are becoming increasingly effective at defining the problems they solve and developing their business models, which investors expect to see validated at a relatively early stage,” Ilinca Păun, founder of Bravva Angels, explained. The team of Bravva speaks with around 15 startups every month, on average. Of these, approximately three are invited to pitch their businesses to the angel investors. The selection criteria include the team’s readiness to scale and raise investment, the size of the market, and the founders’ entrepreneurial stamina. Bravva Angels members are currently assessing 11 new startups for potential investment, following their pitches and in-depth sessions with the teams. Although the community’s portfolio spans multiple sectors, the majority of the companies under consideration are developing SaaS products and operate under B2B, B2B2C, or B2B2B business models. They either target international customers directly or operate in segments of the Romanian market that are large enough to demonstrate traction before moving into their next stage of growth.

data.title: Keller Williams analysis: Romanian property sales fall 17.8%, but disruptions distort data
data.description: Romania recorded 381,094 property transactions in the first nine months of 2026, down 17.8% from 463,592 in the same period of 2025, according to an analysis signed by Keller Williams Romania president Alexandru Văcaru. However, around 80% of the decline occurred in the third quarter, when comparisons were distorted by exceptional events in both years. The first quarter was down 12%, while the second quarter - the only period without major disruptions - was broadly stable, recording a 0.3% increase. June sales were 5.3% higher year over year. By contrast, third-quarter transactions fell 37.9% in 2026. While July 2025 had been unusually strong as buyers rushed to complete purchases before a VAT increase, July 2026 was affected by the shutdown of land-registry platform e-Terra following a cyberattack. Without access to land-registry documents, notaries were unable to authenticate transactions during the outage. Only 11,415 properties were recorded as sold in July 2026, followed by 38,669 in August, according to Keller Williams. September then climbed to 58,353 transactions, up 5.6% year over year, as delayed files were processed and some buyers rushed to meet the September 30 deadline for purchases eligible for the 9% VAT rate. The national figure also conceals significant regional differences. Sibiu county recorded growth of 5.7%, while Brașov county declined by 33%, despite both being affected by the same land-registry disruption. “The market in 2026 is neither collapsing nor clearly recovering,” reads the analysis, recommending that buyers, sellers, and agents examine local figures and months unaffected by exceptional events before making decisions. The final quarter will indicate whether the summer decline represented a temporary interruption or a broader change in market direction, the same source said.

data.title: NATO to send “additional resources” to Black Sea region after attacks on commercial ships in Romania
data.description: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization, or NATO, announced on Tuesday, October 20, that it decided to send “additional resources” to the Black Sea following Russian drone attacks on commercial vessels in the territorial waters of Romania and Bulgaria. The announcement ​came after NATO's main decision-making body, the North Atlantic ​Council, discussed security in the Black Sea at the alliance's ⁠Brussels headquarters the same day. The meeting followed talks between NATO secretary general Mark Rutte and Romanian president Nicușor Dan and Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev on the sidelines of the European Council . Both leaders called for the recent incidents in the Black Sea to be addressed at the Alliance level. https://x.com/NATOpress/status/2112564287776469370 Although the information was provided by a spokesperson who did not specify what type of additional assets would be sent, Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev said that an American reconnaissance aircraft was already patrolling the Black Sea for the “reconnaissance and identification of potential risks.” Soon after, a military analysis website cited by Biziday identified a Boeing P-8 Poseidon from a base in Sicily that carried out a low-altitude search mission off the Bulgarian coast before landing in Varna. This type of aircraft is specialized in naval surveillance and even anti-submarine warfare. Romanian president Nicușor Dan confirmed the military deployment in a post on Facebook , noting that NATO was taking “concrete measures to strengthen security and protect navigation, trade, and energy infrastructure.” “Romania sent a direct message that we expect stronger support through additional counter-drone, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities and expertise, as well as an adapted and strengthened NATO posture in the region. These are essential for protecting lives, global trade, and critical infrastructure, as well as for keeping the Black Sea safe and open,” the official said. Dan reminded that on October 17, two Romanian Air Force F-16 aircraft engaged and shot down two drones that had illegally entered national airspace. Both the Bulgarian and Romanian coasts have been the scene of aerial drone attacks on commercial vessels in recent weeks, and Romanian F-16 aircraft even shot down two Russian attack drones , possibly before they could hit other vessels. In addition to aircraft, drones, and radar systems, NATO members have sent or will send intelligence agents and teams to conduct forensic analysis of explosives, said US Army Colonel Martin Martin L. O'Donnell, a NATO military spokesperson, cited by Reuters . Last ‌week, ⁠seven sailors were reported missing after drones struck two chemical tankers near Romania's Black Sea coast , setting them ablaze and raising fresh security concerns along a vital shipping route used by Ukraine. At ​least five other ​cargo vessels ⁠were hit near the coasts of Romania and neighbouring NATO member Bulgaria over the previous 10 ​days, with at least 23 sailors reported missing or ​dead.

data.title: Ungheni bridge linking Romania and Moldova over Prut River reaches 56% completion
data.description: Construction of the Ungheni bridge across the Prut River has reached 56%, according to the Romanian Road Infrastructure Administration Company (CNAIR). The cross-border project connecting Romania and Moldova is valued at approximately RON 151 million, excluding VAT. “The Ungheni bridge across the Prut has reached a physical completion rate of 56%,” CNAIR announced, adding that the investment is financed with European funds. Romanian contractor Ness Proiect is working on the bridge infrastructure and connecting roads. Current activities include improving the foundation soil and removing topsoil in preparation for subsequent construction stages. “Meanwhile, work on the bridge’s steel deck is continuing on the Moldovan side,” CNAIR said. The contractor has deployed 50 workers and 33 pieces of construction equipment at the site . The contractual deadline for completing the project is December 2027. The bridge will provide a direct connection between Romania’s A8 motorway and Moldova’s road infrastructure, improving transport links between the two countries. It will be the first motorway-standard road bridge built across the Prut since 1989, according to News.ro .

data.title: US bank Goldman Sachs argues Romania’s economy would benefit from currency depreciation
data.description: “Romania’s position suggests that the unsustainable current account deficit is a bigger problem than [its second major macroeconomic challenge], the negative output gap,” the report said, as quoted by Cursdeguvernare.ro . Under these circumstances, the adjustment should combine a weakening of the real effective exchange rate, “possibly through a larger one-off devaluation,” with a more restrictive fiscal policy. According to Goldman Sachs' analysis, Romania is also the economy that deviates the most from the equilibrium zone in the direction of a REER that is too high - a sign that the leu is still overvalued in real terms. The real effective exchange rate index (REER – which takes inflation into account) calculated by CFA Romania reached 122.2 in January 2026, the highest level since the series began in 1994, and stood at 118.7 in July - about 19% above the average for the period 2010–2019. Over the same period, the nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) changed very little (101.5 in July 2026).

data.title: Romanian Business Leaders oppose proposal requiring lawyers for certain company contracts
data.description: RBL argued that the measure would increase the administrative burden, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), running counter to the European Commission’s targets of reducing administrative costs by at least 25% for all companies and 35% for SMEs. “Legislative proposal B563/2026 [...] would oblige companies to use a lawyer for company incorporation and amendment documents, as well as for contracts for which the law requires written form, including addenda,” RBL said, as reported by Economica.net . The association estimated that the additional cost would exceed EUR 100 million annually for company documents and standard commercial contracts alone. If the requirement were interpreted broadly to include employment contracts, the cost could approach EUR 800 million per year. UNBR disputed both the interpretation and the cost estimates, arguing that the proposal would not require a lawyer for every company contract. The obligation would apply only to contracts for which the law requires written form under private signature for validity or proof, subject to legal exceptions.  Simply concluding a contract in writing would not automatically trigger the requirement, and non-compliance would not invalidate the contract unless the law expressly provided for that sanction, UNBR said. The lawyers’ organisation also considers RBL’s cost estimates unrealistic, arguing that they fail to account for the documents actually covered, applicable exemptions, legal services already contracted and genuine additional costs. It said the EUR 800 million scenario relies on an interpretation that goes beyond the proposal’s scope. UNBR acknowledged that concerns about costs, simpler procedures and legislative predictability are legitimate. However, it argued that the amendment could also simplify representation procedures by eliminating additional powers of attorney requested solely to confirm a representative’s authority. The applicable legal requirements would remain in force, but businesses could benefit from fewer trips, lower costs and shorter delays.

data.title: Romania’s incoming PSD government wants thorough report on current financial situation
data.description: “Based on the information I have, much of which is public, the financial situation appears to be very difficult,” Grindeanu said, as reported by B1tv.ro . He accused the outgoing government of deferring expenditure to keep the budget deficit down. “It is easy to boast about a small deficit when you have not paid your bills or covered the state’s essential operating expenses by the end of the year,” the PSD leader said. Asked where the money for not one but two planned budget rectifications would come from, Grindeanu replied: “I am not the prime minister. Mr Luca Niculescu will answer these questions, and the line ministers will respond on their respective areas. What I said earlier, however, is that we need to start with something else before the rectification: presenting the situation. The up-to-date financial situation must first be presented in Parliament. We have set a two-week deadline.” Romania’s Ministry of Finance published the budget execution figures for January–September at the end of last week, after releasing public debt data through the end of July. Romania’s public deficit widened slightly in Q3, but remained moderate in January–September. The general government budget deficit contracted by 23% y/y to RON 78.5 billion (EUR 14.7 billion) in January–September, accounting for 3.8% of GDP, down from 5.3% of GDP in the same period of 2025. Preliminary data discussed at a government meeting on October 16 indicate a slight deterioration in budget execution in Q3, but this does not put the full-year deficit target of 6.2% of GDP at risk. The target is 1.45 percentage points (pp) below the 7.65% recorded in 2025. Romania’s debt-to-GDP ratio remains below 60% at end-July. Romania’s gross public debt, measured under the EU’s ESA methodology, increased by RON 67.7 billion year-to-date through the end of July, equivalent to EUR 12.9 billion at the current exchange rate, according to the latest data published by the Finance Ministry. The debt-to-GDP ratio reached 59.8%, up from 58.9% at the end of 2025, based on our calculations using revised GDP figures. The dynamics of public debt and the debt-to-GDP ratio during the first seven months of 2026 reveal three notable aspects: the revised debt-to-GDP trajectory is now entirely below the 60% threshold; the ratio increased by only 0.9 percentage points during the period; and the entire increase in public debt was generated by foreign-currency-denominated debt, while debt denominated in local currency remained broadly unchanged.

data.title: Romania’s construction volume up 40% y/y in August
data.description: The unusually high growth rate was partly due to a base effect, as contractors brought forward works in July 2025 to avoid the harsher tax regime introduced in August 2025. However, the sector’s robust performance cannot be attributed entirely to the base effect. The construction volume index accelerated from 7.7% y/y in Q1 to 18.0% y/y in Q2, reaching an average growth rate of 18.6% y/y in July–August. The record level of construction activity this year, supported by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), particularly in civil engineering and non-residential construction, creates high base effects that erode the potential for further growth in 2027. In value-added terms, the sector’s annual growth accelerated from 7.8% y/y in Q1 to 15.4% y/y in Q2. In July–August, as in each of the two previous quarters, residential construction outperformed the other segments. Output rose by an average of 28.3% y/y over the two months (+54.8% y/y in August alone), following growth of 15% y/y in Q1 and 25% y/y in Q2. In seasonally and working-day-adjusted (swda) terms, residential construction output reached a new record in August. In fact, all three market segments reached new highs in August, even though total construction volume remained slightly below the record level reached in July 2025. This counterintuitive result reflects the separate seasonal adjustments applied to each market segment and to the market total. Over the past five years, civil engineering has expanded the most. Its volume more than doubled on average in July–August compared with the same period five years earlier, against a more modest 17% increase in residential construction and a 71.4% rise in non-residential construction. Civil engineering activity has been visibly driven by projects funded under the RRF, and robust growth is expected to continue over the remainder of the year.

data.title: Moody’s welcomes new government in Romania, recalls budget is key
data.description: On October 20, Romania's Parliament approved the minority government controlled by the Social Democrats (PSD) but headed by independent prime minister Luca Niculescu. The update offers a positive note after Moody’s warned on October 1, following the third failed attempt to form a government in Romania, of a significant risk of snap elections and the absence of a 2027 budget by year-end. However, some of the concerns raised by Moody’s on October 1 remain valid: much of the improvement in the budget deficit reflected temporary restrictions on public-sector wages and social transfers, and further measures are needed to continue reducing Romania’s deficit. The agency highlighted that fiscal adjustment remains difficult and that Romania will have to manage several pressures in the coming period, including rising interest and personnel expenses and additional defence needs. Moody’s also stressed the need to continue structural reforms that contribute to stabilising public debt and improving its sustainability. Romania’s Finance Ministry, which will remain under the supervision of Alexandru Nazare, said the Moody’s update was a call “for responsibility and continuity”. “The 2027 budget will be a major test of credibility: it must be built on realistic revenues, clear priorities and expenditure that the state can effectively support. Given that financing needs remain high, budgetary discipline is not optional, but a mandatory condition for protecting the country’s rating, maintaining creditors’ confidence and preserving Romania’s capacity to finance its development,” finance minister Alexandru Nazare said. Moody’s maintained the budget deficit trajectory set out in its August 7 sovereign update and anticipated continued fiscal adjustment. The agency estimated that the ESA deficit will decline from 7.9% of GDP in 2025 to 5.8% in 2026 and 5.5% in 2027. The government has pledged to bring the cash deficit down to 5.3% of GDP. The ESA deficit would probably be 0.1–0.2 percentage points higher. At the same time, the primary deficit is expected to decline gradually to 2.7% of GDP in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027. In ESA terms, Moody’s deficit trajectory is more demanding than the figures cited by S&P. Moody’s projects a deficit of 5.8% of GDP in 2026 and 5.5% in 2027, while S&P’s baseline scenario envisages deficits of 6.25% and 5.8%, respectively. S&P, however, has used this baseline as a benchmark for potential rating actions, with better-than-expected fiscal performance potentially supporting an upgrade and weaker performance weighing in the opposite direction.

data.title: EU, Moldovan leaders congratulate Romania’s new PM
data.description: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen and European Parliament president Roberta Metsola congratulated Luca Niculescu after he took office as Romania’s prime minister on Tuesday, October 20. Moreover, Moldova’s leader Maia Sandu and prime minister Vasile Tofan also welcomed the new government and pledged continued cooperation. “We have important work ahead of us,” von der Leyen wrote on X, citing the need to create opportunities for citizens and businesses and strengthen security on Europe’s Eastern Flank. “We have no time to waste. Let’s move forward together, for Romania and for Europe,” she added. https://x.com/vonderleyen/status/2112575421170524652?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw In her turn, Roberta Metsola said Romania had an important role in shaping Europe’s future at a time when security and the need for a stronger, more united EU were increasingly important. https://x.com/EP_President/status/2112576732356108738?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2112576732356108738%7Ctwgr%5E278459c4c048e81256bc1130a77fc32b99383484%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mediafax.ro%2Fpolitic%2Froberta-metsola-l-a-felicitat-pe-luca-niculescu-dupa-investire-romania-are-un-rol-important-in-conturarea-viitorului-european-23829014 Moldova’s president Maia Sandu also published a message on social media, wishing Luca Niculescu and his government success and thanking outgoing prime minister Ilie Bolojan for their cooperation. “Romania can always count on us,” she said. https://x.com/sandumaiamd/status/2112557276296810501?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw Meanwhile, Moldovan prime minister Vasile Tofan described Romania as a reliable partner connected to Moldova through language, culture, and close ties between communities on both sides of the Prut River. He highlighted bilateral projects in energy, infrastructure, and European integration, adding that the government in Chișinău would remain “a trusted partner and a friend” to Bucharest. https://x.com/Vasile_Tofan/status/2112566242171048432?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2112566242171048432%7Ctwgr%5E17782c251d3f93b914c879989765f77c20a9f1e8%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.digi24.ro%2Fstiri%2Factualitate%2Fpolitica%2Fmaia-sandu-si-premierul-vasile-tofan-ii-ureaza-succes-lui-luca-niculescu-si-asigura-ca-romania-poate-conta-oricand-pe-r-moldova-4001475 The Romanian Parliament approved Luca Niculescu’s cabinet on October 20 with 280 votes in favor and 58 against, ending more than five months of political deadlock. The independent diplomat was president Nicușor Dan’s fourth nominee for prime minister following three unsuccessful attempts to form a government. The new 18-member cabinet, comprising 11 Social Democrat (PSD) ministers and seven independents, was sworn in later that day and held its first meeting. Niculescu told ministers that improving Romanians’ standard of living would be the government’s main priority. Its immediate tasks include revising the 2026 budget, drafting next year’s budget, preparing for winter, and addressing potential problems in the energy sector. “We may sometimes come from different worlds - some of you are politicians, while others are only now discovering this world - but we are nevertheless a team,” Niculescu said . He urged ministers to use the governing program as the basis for their decisions.

data.title: A seasoned IHG luxury leader takes the helm of one of Romania's most celebrated hotels
data.description: InterContinental Athénée Palace Bucharest announces the appointment of Angelo Zuccala as General Manager of the hotel. Mr Zuccala will continue to also serve as Area General Manager IHG Hotels & Resorts Southern Europe Luxury & Lifestyle , combining the leadership of the Bucharest landmark with a regional role in IHG's luxury portfolio. Mr. Zuccala brings more than 30 years of international hospitality experience, most of it with IHG's InterContinental brand, which he joined in the early 2000s. His career in luxury hotels has taken him through the UK, France, Egypt, Malta, Germany, Romania, Bulgaria and Montenegro, in roles spanning sales, luxury event management, revenue management, food and beverage, concept development, operational excellence and general management. He previously led the former InterContinental Bucharest hotel, Crowne Plaza Bucharest and, more recently, InterContinental Sofia and Regent brand in Montenegro. He holds a Master's degree in Business Studies and Finance from Excelia Group, La Rochelle, France and is a French and Italian national. "It is a true privilege and a great source of pride to take the helm of InterContinental Athénée Palace Bucharest. This is a hotel with extraordinary heritage and a rich history, recognised internationally with numerous awards, and one of the most distinguished properties in the IHG luxury portfolio. It is an honor for me to build on this legacy, to acknowledge and further refine the exceptional standards of our teams and to keep writing the next chapter of this iconic hotel together with our guests, partners and the city of Bucharest." said Angelo Zuccala. "I would like to thank ANA Hotels for their vision and the substantial investment made in recent years. It has transformed the hotel into a true jewel of the InterContinental portfolio, and it gives us an exceptional foundation to build on." added Mr. Zuccala. "InterContinental Athénée Palace Bucharest is a landmark of luxury hospitality in Romania and a symbol of Bucharest's hotel heritage. The investments made in modernising the hotel reflect ANA Hotels' commitment to preserving and enhancing this legacy while delivering experiences that meet the highest international standards. We are delighted to welcome Mr Angelo Zuccala back to Bucharest. His appointment as General Manager marks a new chapter in the hotel's evolution, offering an opportunity to further strengthen its positioning in the international luxury market and to continue its development alongside our partner, IHG Hotels & Resorts." said Meda Vasiliu, Chief Operating Officer of ANA Hotels. InterContinental Athénée Palace Bucharest, a storied landmark of the city's history and hospitality and a Michelin key holder for the second year in a row, has been awarded, at the recent World Luxury Awards Gala held on October 17, three continental and regional-level awards: Best Luxury Hotel & Conference Centre , Europe Best Luxury Urban Hotel , Eastern Europe Best Luxury Cultural Hotel , Eastern Europe The hotel features JORJ Restaurant, The English Bar, Café Athénée and Spa InterContinental, along with the historical Le Diplomate Ballroom, part of the national heritage. The hotel is owned by ANA Hotels and operated under the InterContinental® Hotels & Resorts brand, part of IHG Hotels & Resorts' luxury portfolio.

data.title: Romanian DIICOT prosecutors seize some properties of developer Nordis a third time
data.description: DIICOT prosecutors once again placed the apartments constructed and owned by infamous developer Norids in Mamaia, on the Romanian Black Sea coast, under seizure, after the Bucharest Court of Appeal lifted the measure last week, according to a statement from the Prosecutor’s Office made public on Tuesday, October 20. In total, prosecutors seized 155 apartments, 8 parking spaces, 4 commercial spaces, a basement and 2 storage units that are unfinished, as well as 14 plots of land, valued at EUR 12 million. “The measure was taken as a continuation of the criminal investigation activities carried out in the case, in view of the extensions of the criminal investigation for the offense of fraud with particularly serious consequences ordered on October 10, 2025, and August 18, 2026, corresponding to 363 new criminal complaints filed by injured individuals or legal entities against the suspects and defendants, both individuals and legal entities, with total reported damages exceeding EUR 58 million,” the prosecutors said in a press release . On October 15, 2026, the Bucharest Court of Appeal ruled in a final judgment to lift the precautionary seizure on Nordis apartments in Mamaia worth more than EUR 100 million. The court admitted only the appeals filed by Nordis Management and Nordis Mamaia and rejected the appeal of Nordis owner Vladimir Ciorbă, keeping the latter’s assets still frozen. Background In February 2025, Nordis owners Emanuel Poștoacă and Vladimir Ciorbă, the latter's wife, former PSD MP Laura Vicol, and others were detained by DIICOT on charges including forming an organized criminal group, embezzlement, money laundering, tax evasion, and fraud. They allegedly collected EUR 195 million from Nordis clients , people who wanted to buy apartments in residential complexes developed by Nordis and paid in advance, and embezzled more than EUR 70 million. The arrests were later overturned by the Romanian High Court . In August, the Bucharest Court of Appeal lifted almost EUR 90 million in asset seizures imposed by prosecutors on real estate assets, as well as on the accounts and shares held by Nordis owners Vladimir Ciorbă, Florin Alexandru Poștoacă, legal director Camelia Bîndiu and the group's parent company, Nordis Management. Around the same time, prosecutors expanded the investigation into Nordis. After hundreds of new complaints were filed against Nordis, prosecutors reinstated the seizure measures on Nordis apartments worth more than EUR 64 million. The seizure was confirmed by the court on November 14, 2025. So far, approximately 700 criminal complaints have been filed in the Nordis case, involving 850 people who have victim status in the case, while the total damages calculated by prosecutors amount to EUR 75 million. The properties concerned are ones that prosecutors allege were sold but never built or delivered.

data.title: Luca Niculescu confirmed as Romania’s new prime minister, ending five months of political uncertainty
data.description: Independent Luca Niculescu was invested as Romania’s new prime minister on Tuesday, October 20, in a joint plenary session. According to the official announcement, out of a total of 464 members of Parliament, 355 senators and deputies were present. A total of 338 valid votes were recorded, of which 280 were “for” and 58 were against. As such, the Niculescu government easily passed the threshold of 233 votes needed to be invested. “We are getting straight to work; we will hold the first government meeting this evening; Romania can no longer wait,” prime minister Luca Niculescu announced after Parliament’s vote. The new prime minister and his ministers will next be sworn in before president Nicușor Dan, after which the new government can formally take office. Niculescu’s 18-member cabinet replaces the Liberal-led Ilie Bolojan government, dismissed on May 5 . The new government includes 11 ministers from the Social Democratic Party (PSD), many of them returning ministers, and seven independents. Before the vote, PSD, the National Liberal Party (PNL), the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR), the national minorities group, and the United for Romania parliamentary group announced their support for the cabinet. Together, the parties mobilized 279 votes, comfortably above the 233 required for confirmation.

data.title: Romania’s Competition Council approves Raiffeisen’s acquisition of Garanti Bank
data.description: The Competition Council, the body that safeguards consumer interests in Romania, authorized the transaction through which Raiffeisen Bank intends to acquire Garanti Bank and Motoractive IFN, according to a statement made public on Tuesday, October 20. Raiffeisen Bank announced in March that it would acquire Garanti BBVA's business in Romania for EUR 591 million (USD 680 million), its first significant acquisition in several years. In its analysis, the Competition Council found that the transaction does not raise significant obstacles to effective competition in the Romanian market or in a substantial part of it, and that there are no serious doubts regarding its compatibility with a normal competitive environment. Following the acquisition, Raiffeisen will become Romania's third-largest bank by total assets and intends to integrate the business into its existing local operations, the banking group said. Motoractive IFN, part of the Garanti BBVA Romania Group, is a non-bank financial institution that provides, under the Garanti BBVA Leasing brand, financial leasing solutions for vehicles, equipment, and real estate, according to Economica . Raiffeisen also purchased Motoractive Multiservices, which provides fleet administration and management services under the Garanti BBVA Fleet Management brand, as part of the deal. Garanti, listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange, is a subsidiary of Spanish group BBVA, which estimated that the transaction would have a positive net impact of approximately 10 basis points on its Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio and EUR 112 million on the group's income statement. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. A gradual integration process will then begin, which, according to current estimates, is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027. Raiffeisen intends to merge the acquired entities with its Romanian operations. Until this process is completed, the two entities will continue to operate independently.

data.title: Logistics real estate developer CTP leases 55,600 sqm to Pepco at CTPark Bucharest West
data.description: CTP, a major European owner, developer and manager of logistics and industrial real estate, announced a lease with discount retailer Pepco for 55,619 sqm at CTPark Bucharest West in Romania on Tuesday, October 20. The location is the largest industrial park in continental Europe, with nearly 1.5 million sqm of planned lettable space. Located to the west of Bucharest along the A1 motorway, it provides direct access to Romania’s capital and key transport corridors serving the country and the wider region. The park houses a cluster of retailers, manufacturers and third-party logistics providers serving both domestic and international markets. The site also has CTP Clubhaus, an on-site community hub providing amenities including a restaurant, supermarket, meeting spaces, outdoor fitness areas and medical services, supporting employee wellbeing and helping occupiers attract and retain staff, and network with each other. Pepco will operate a regional distribution center from the facility, serving the Romanian market and the wider Central Eastern Europe (CEE) region. Having previously occupied the building through a third-party logistics provider, the retailer has now entered a direct partnership with CTP. “Pepco choosing CTPark Bucharest West reflects the strategic importance of the location, while the switch over to a long-term direct lease structure confirms a strong relationship, which we are grateful for. We have been able to work closely with Pepco to create a solution tailored to their individual operational requirements and to support their distribution network,” said Andrei Marian, Business Development Director, CTP Romania. CTP has a portfolio of 14.8 million sqm of GLA in 12 countries and 2.0 million sqm under construction as of 30 June 2026. The company signed a record 1.8 million sqm of leases across its portfolio year-to-date as of August 2026.

data.title: Madrigal Choir announces 10-concert Christmas tour across Romania
data.description: Romania’s Madrigal - Marin Constantin National Chamber Choir will hold its 2026 Christmas tour from December 3 through 22. Conducted by Anna Ungureanu, the choir will give 10 performances in Brașov, Cluj-Napoca, Timișoara, Oradea, Constanța, Tulcea, Bucharest, and Craiova. The tour will begin with two performances at Brașov’s Sică Alexandrescu Theater on December 3 and 4, with the second already sold out. It will continue in Cluj-Napoca on December 6, Timișoara on December 8, and Oradea on December 10. Further concerts are scheduled in Constanța on December 12 and Tulcea on December 13. Details for the Constanța performance will be announced later. In Bucharest, the choir will present two separate productions at the Aula Magna of the Polytechnic University: Christmas of the Flowers on December 16 and Christmas Mood on December 17. The tour will conclude at Craiova’s Polyvalent Hall on December 22. Most performances will use the Madrigal Christmas: Two Concerts in One Show format, according to the official announcement. The performances are recommended for audiences older than 7. Tickets are available through Entertix and the Madrigal Choir’s website.

data.title: Climate Change Summit brings 2,100 participants to Bucharest, announces 2027 rebranding
data.description: The fifth edition of the Climate Change Summit, an annual event highlighting energy security, access to resources, and economic competitiveness in Romania and beyond, brought over 2,000 participants to Bucharest on October 14. Under the theme “The Infrastructures of the Future,” the event, connected international perspectives with Romania’s and the region’s economic and social challenges. In particular, discussions at this edition of the Summit tackled the green transition, energy security, access to water and food, and Romania’s ability to respond to climate risks. At the opening of Climate Change Summit 2026, Romanian president Nicușor Dan delivered a message highlighting the event’s role in connecting public institutions, researchers, the business community, and civil society. He also emphasized the importance of integrating nature protection into development decisions and collaborating with civil society, mentioning the Bucharest–Ilfov Green Belt , Roșia Montană, the conservation of the Lake Techirghiol area, and support for wildlife rehabilitation centers. The third edition of the “State of the Climate 2026” report for Romania, prepared by InfoClima researchers, was presented at the Climate Change Summit. Topics covered include vulnerabilities in the energy system, the effects of heatwaves on health, and the role of emissions reductions in limiting the intensification of extreme heat. The effects of heat are also reflected in public health: according to the report, approximately 2,879 deaths in Romania were attributed to heat during June–September 2025. According to the same report, since 2007, Romania has had an interministerial plan of measures for heatwave periods, but it does not have a heat-and-health action plan in line with the World Health Organization’s approach, including mortality surveillance, registers of vulnerable people, and an assessment of measures. Issues addressed Discussions on the Blue Stage – Global Perspective and Green Stage – Regional Impact addressed the relationship between climate, the economy, and geopolitics, infrastructure financing, resource use, and Romania’s potential in advanced green technologies. Gianpiero Nacci, Managing Director, Climate Strategy and Delivery at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, presented the institution’s perspective on financing the transition in Central and Eastern Europe: “Mobilizing human capital is essential to driving the transition.” Gareth Stapleton, associate researcher and climate ambassador at the University of Reading, analyzed the obstacles preventing climate finance from reaching the project implementation stage. Investments in natural capital were discussed by Manon Mura, Associate Director, Investor Relations UK & Europe at New Forests. During the discussion on the Green Stage, Iuliana Tiba, Director of Environmental, Social and Positive Impact Financing at BRD, highlighted demand for financing energy efficiency and renewable energy, while Nacci and Mura discussed the risks and opportunities associated with investments. Meanwhile, Jennifer Gilberg, head of Bayer’s Crop Science division in Romania, Bulgaria, and the Republic of Moldova, and Managing Director of Bayer Romania, addressed agriculture’s dual responsibility: producing food and responding to climate change. International guests also included Juliette Lassman, an OECD policy analyst specializing in water governance and the circular economy; Esteban Arriaga Miranda, CEO of the European Food Banks Federation (FEBA); and Boyana Achovski, CEO of ATMIX and former Secretary General of Gas Infrastructure Europe. The 2026 edition also explored how competition for resources, scientific progress, and technological innovation are transforming the European economy. André Månberger of Lund University and Jiayi Zhou, a researcher at the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, discussed critical raw material security and new geopolitical dependencies. At the same time, experts from research, the business community, and public institutions analyzed Romania’s potential to develop advanced green technologies and turn research results into competitive solutions. The agenda also included perspectives on human longevity, through a presentation by João Pedro de Magalhães of the University of Birmingham on the impact of extreme environmental conditions on health and lifespan. Climate Change Summit becomes Change Summit in 2027 The fifth edition also marked the beginning of a new stage: starting in 2027, Climate Change Summit will become Change Summit, expanding discussions from climate challenges to a broader range of transformations shaping the future of the economy and society. According to the organizers, climate change, technological progress, geopolitical tensions, demographic developments, and economic transformations can no longer be understood separately. Change Summit will explore eight major forces shaping the future: AI and technology, geopolitical transformations, climate action, the economy of the next decade, people and society, the cities of the future, science that changes the world, and leadership in an unstable world. Climate will remain a central component of the platform, alongside new perspectives on competitiveness, technology, science, and the future of society. The first edition of Change Summit will take place on October 27, 2027, under the theme “Understanding the Forces Shaping Our Future.”

data.title: PwC PayWell: Salary growth in Romania’s private sector still slow
data.description: Private companies in Romania expect base salaries to rise by an average of 5.65% in 2027, following increases of 6.67% in 2026 and 7.47% in 2025, continuing a slowdown in wage growth, according to a PwC PayWell 2026 study. The slowdown comes against a difficult economic backdrop. According to the National Institute of Statistics (INS), Romania’s GDP fell by 0.7% year on year in the first half of 2026 (unadjusted data), and the economy stagnated in the second quarter compared with the first. At the same time, although inflation has eased in recent months, it continues to erode employees’ purchasing power and put pressure on companies to adjust salaries. The average inflation rate over the past 12 months stands at 9.5%, above this year’s average base salary increase. However, the National Bank of Romania (BNR) expects inflation to fall to 6.1% by the end of this year and to 3.4% by the end of 2027. If these forecasts prove accurate, the salary increases companies expect for next year would outpace inflation. “Salary growth in recent years has not been backed by higher productivity. Romania is becoming less and less competitive in terms of labor costs. Even though demand for staff has cooled along with the economy, demographic pressures are structural and will become acute again once growth resumes. A sustainable balance can only be restored by raising skill levels, which can support productivity and competitiveness in the long term, especially in a technology-driven economy,” said Oana Munteanu, Director, Workforce Leader, PwC Romania. In 2026, the largest increases in average base salary were in business process outsourcing and shared service centers (BPO/SSC), at 8.19%, followed by banking, at 6.82%. At the other end of the scale, technology, which led the ranking in 2025, recorded the smallest increase this year, at 2.88%. However, it remains the sector with the highest average gross monthly salary in the study, at RON 21,744. For 2027, technology companies expect the largest increase in average salary, at 6.56%, followed by retail companies, at 6.40%. By business function, the largest salary increases in 2026 were in IT (10.66%), legal (9.47%), and strategic planning (9.20%). These functions exist in companies across many sectors and are also the best paid in the sample. According to the same study, a pay gap in favor of men is widest for high salaries (11.9%) and drops below 5% for mid- range salaries (4.7%). The gap is narrowing compared with previous years: for high salaries, it was 14% in 2024 and 12.9% in 2025. There were no significant changes for mid-range and low salaries. The largest gender pay gaps are still found in banking and technology, although both have narrowed since 2025. In industry and hospitality, women are paid the same as men, or slightly more. Age is also a factor when it comes to wages. In the sample, employees aged 26 to 43 have the highest salaries, closely followed by those aged 44 to 54. Pay is lower both for employees at the start of their careers, which is explained by their level of seniority, and for those over 55, a group that unfortunately has fewer opportunities for career progression and job mobility. According to the study, employees rated as high performers earn 18–27% more than their peers. Regionally, Bucharest-Ilfov has the highest average gross monthly salary in the sample, at RON 17,239. This is almost double the level in Muntenia, around 80% higher than in Moldavia and 52% higher than in Banat and Transylvania. Regional gaps are wider for management positions and narrower for operational roles, largely because management roles are concentrated in the capital. Aside from salary increases, extra days off are the most common benefit offered by the companies in the study (81%), followed by meal vouchers (78%). Other widespread benefits include private healthcare plans and free coffee and soft drinks. Compared with 2025, fewer companies now offer meal vouchers, reimbursement of holiday expenses, cultural activities, reimbursement for glasses, and gym memberships. By contrast, more companies offer in-office massages, tech devices, additional maternity leave benefits, and coaching. The PayWell study is based on data from more than 140 participating companies in seven sectors, covering over 198,000 employees and more than 1,400 distinct job positions.

data.title: Romanian cosmetics manufacturer Farmec appoints Ioana Birta as General Manager
data.description: Farmec, one of Romania’s oldest cosmetics manufacturers, announced the appointment of Ioana Birta as General Manager, following a decision by the Board of Directors, on Tuesday, October 20. The appointment is part of a larger corporate restructuring. The company was previously led by Mircea Turdean, “who, since 2010, has played an essential role in strengthening the company’s market position and defining its growth directions. In this new stage, Mircea Turdean will continue to contribute to the company’s development by being involved in setting strategic directions as a member of the Board of Directors.” Farmec’s Board of Directors will retain its current composition, with Ovidiu Horea Turdean as chairman, Mircea Liviu Turdean as member, and Lucian Pîntea as member. Responsibility for setting the company’s strategy and development directions rests exclusively with the members of the Board of Directors. The new General Manager will be responsible for executive management and implementing the strategy approved by the Board of Directors. Ioana Birta’s priorities include modernizing processes, increasing operational efficiency, strengthening collaboration between departments, and enhancing Farmec’s competitiveness in a market characterized by intense competition and continuously evolving consumer expectations. “Farmec has important strengths: strong brands, tradition and expertise in the cosmetics industry, and people who have contributed to the company’s development over the years. My priority is to leverage these strengths through more efficient processes, better integration of activities, and decisions based on economic performance. I want us to build on what is working well and strengthen Farmec’s long-term competitiveness,” said Ioana Birta, General Manager of Farmec. Ioana Birta has experience in strategy, business development, corporate finance, and operational management. Her professional career includes work in auditing and consulting at a Big Four firm and the role of CFO of the TeraPlast Group, where she coordinated investment projects, acquisitions, and strategic transactions. She subsequently expanded her responsibilities to include commercial and operational management. Since September 2025, she has been part of Farmec’s management team as Operations Director, contributing to process modernization and improvements in the company’s performance. Ioana is a CFA Charterholder and an ACCA Fellow. Farmec is one of Romania’s leading cosmetics manufacturers, with a tradition spanning more than 135 years. The company’s portfolio includes well-known brands such as Gerovital, Farmec, and Aslavital, and its activities include the production and sale of cosmetics and personal care products.

data.title: US Restores Intelligence to Ukraine as Witkoff Carries Peace Proposals to Putin

According to the Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, Oleksandr Hanzha, the casualties came in a strike on warehouses near Dnipro, while drone and artillery fire also hit the Synelynkove, Nikopol and Kryvyi Rih districts.

data.title: Japan Lifts 5-Year Restrictions on Ukrainian Poultry, Egg Imports

The decision was formally agreed upon on Oct. 16, and it opens a new market for Ukrainian producers, while adding to growing cooperation between Kyiv and Tokyo.

data.title: Hungary Blocks Ukraine’s Next EU Step Despite Reset – Report
data.description: Hungary refused to approve a procedural step toward opening Ukraine’s final two EU negotiating clusters, European Pravda reported, citing diplomats. The reported objection follows last week’s breakthrough on two other clusters and talks aimed at rebuilding Kyiv-Budapest relations. Ukraine and Ireland’s EU presidency aim to open the remaining clusters before the end of 2026.

data.title: Trust in Zelensky Rises to 57% After US Pressure, Poll Finds
data.description: A new Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) poll found that 57% of respondents trusted President Volodymyr Zelensky in interviews conducted Oct. 10-16, up from 43% in a smaller group surveyed on Oct. 8-9. KIIS said the increase likely reflects a “rally-around-the-flag” effect after the US-Russia diesel deal and pressure on Ukraine. In the overall October survey, 54% said they trusted Zelensky and 41% did not.

data.title: NAZA: When technology makes killing a calculation
data.description: GOA, India – There are films that recount the horrors of war, films that make audiences feel the pain of those who endure it, and films that take us somewhere far more disturbing: into the machinery that makes such horrors possible. NAZA, the documentary by Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, belongs to this third category. It asks us to look beyond the images of destruction that have become tragically familiar from Gaza and confront the systems, institutional cultures and technological processes through which the destruction of human life can be organised, assessed and justified.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. data.title: APANHA-SE MAIS DEPRESSA UM MENTIROSO QUE UM COXO!
data.description:
DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE
PERSISTENTE. BÔ DISSAL I NA BIN FASSI PASSSAÇÃO LI. tUDO PUBLICAÇÕES KU I FASSI
I NA RESP+UNDI PAREL. NIN IKANA SEDU DIDIA. NONA VINGAL MANERA KU NÓ PUDI. JÁ
TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU
AGRESSÃO E NESTE MOMENTO ESTÁ EM QUELUZ EM PORTUGAL. FILHO DA PUTA. MENTIROSO
COMO OS TEUS PATRÕES OS SUJOS JOMAV E BRAIMA CAMARÁ. MARCOS GALINA, BU NA
ARREPENDI. PERA BU DJUBI. ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E
COMPRAS?! VAMOS PROVAR DEPOIS. FIDJU DI BALETA Olá a todos, ainda bem que descobriram
que o Pirata informático- hackec é o Marcos Galina Barbosa, Eng. Informático.
Tentei várias vezes avisar o Ticha Aly Silva mas ele não respondeu e nem deu
importância julgo eu. No tempo da campanha para a liderança do Paigc, este
indivíduo era um fervoroso apoiante do Bá Quecuto no Facebook e a técnica que
usava era o envio de Phishing aos apoiantes do Dsp, recolhia informações
pessoais das pessoas que posteriormente eram expostas no Blog do Doka. Tentou
comigo mas não resultou. Tenham cuidado com este sujeito que está nas mãos de
B. Camara. Outra coisa, gostaria de conhecer a vossa página no Fecebook. Estamos Juntos. AC Nota GP: Até jovens inocentes,
Lesmes, Masta Tito e demais outros, os tais vendidos e comprados foram as tuas
vítimas. teu filho da puta que o bandido de Baciro Djá trouxe para Bissau para funções no aparelho de Estado e dizes que outros recebem favores.
Desde quando é que és mais honesto ou
mais competentes que os outros? Pagas e até pode ser com a tua vida para
perceberes as irresponsabilidades
dos teus actos. Publicada por O

Camaradas, em vez de continuarmos a aceitar essa humilhação, já é tempo de acordar para libertarmos desses politicos malvados que só pensam neles e lutarmos ao lado dos verdadeiros interesses do POVO! data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP não respeita os antigos combatentes e sempre usou e abusou desses camaradas. Prova disso é que continuou a governar mesmo já com Carlos Correia como primeiro ministro. Usou até o cadáver de Carmem Perreira para promover sua imagem, pois é sabido que a malograda como sendo antigo combatente e membro do PAIGC o corpo só deveria passar por ANP e sede do partido e nunca na Primatura como aconteceu, e por cima de tudo com indivíduos alí barricados por vontade própria vandalizando instituição do estado o que demonstra uma clara promoção ao anarquismo. Não respeitou nem o Pai da Nação(ALC), nem o PR quanto mais o formalismo de um estado de direito democrático, prova disso mais uma vez, o ganancioso após o PR ter depositado coroas de flores no túmulo de ALC no dia dos heróis nacionais, reuniu os seus "gangs" para o mesmo efeito, conseguiu até mobilizar um dos familiares do Pai da Nação para lhe acompanhar tudo isso para manipular e dividir os guineenses "guineenses ku udjus fitchadu" para os seus intereses obscuros.

Hij vindt dat bureaucratie en een beperkte uitvoeringscapaciteit de uitvoering van het beleid vertragen. Vooral ouderen, jongeren en mensen met een beperking moeten volgens hem sneller concrete verbeteringen merken. Reyme benadrukt dat de bevolking de coalitie uiteindelijk op haar resultaten zal beoordelen. The post Reyme vindt dat regering te langzaam resultaten boekt appeared first on Suriname Herald .

data.title: Bouva en Ramdin bespreken extra technische steun voor Suriname
data.description: Suriname wil nauwer samenwerken met de Organisatie van Amerikaanse Staten (OAS), vooral bij de versterking van overheidsinstituties en technische ondersteuning. Minister Melvin Bouva besprak deze mogelijkheden met OAS-secretaris-generaal Albert Ramdin in Washington D.C. Ook de situatie in Haïti, economische uitdagingen in de regio en het aantrekken van duurzame investeringen kwamen ter sprake. The post Bouva en Ramdin bespreken extra technische steun voor Suriname appeared first on Suriname Herald .

data.title: Slangenhoutstraat tot donderdag deels afgesloten door rioleringswerkzaamheden
data.description: Weggebruikers moeten nog tot donderdag rekening houden met een gedeeltelijke afsluiting van de Slangenhoutstraat. Kuldipsingh Infra N.V. vervangt de riolering om de afwatering te verbeteren en wateroverlast tegen te gaan. Het bedrijf verwacht het afgesloten weggedeelte op 22 oktober weer open te stellen, maar de werkzaamheden aan de riolering langs de weg gaan daarna verder. data.title: Plein wil maandelijkse financiële steun voor slachtoffers vervuiling Saramaccarivier
data.description: Al ongeveer vier maanden verkeren bewoners langs de Saramaccarivier volgens NPS-parlementariër Ivanildo Plein in onzekerheid over hun levensonderhoud. Door de vervuiling kunnen zij de rivier niet zoals voorheen gebruiken voor onder meer visvangst en dagelijkse werkzaamheden. Plein vindt dat voedselpakketten alleen niet genoeg zijn en wil dat de regering de getroffen gezinnen tijdelijk maandelijks financiële steun geeft. The post Plein wil maandelijkse financiële steun voor slachtoffers vervuiling Saramaccarivier appeared first on Suriname Herald .

data.title: Woning volledig in vlammen opgegaan na overslaande grasbrand
data.description: Een grasbrand aan de Papitodostraat heeft maandagmiddag een woning volledig in de as gelegd. Het vuur sloeg over naar het nabijgelegen pand van ongeveer 5 bij 6 meter, dat grotendeels uit hout en zinkplaten bestond. Alleen het aangebouwde bad- en toiletgedeelte bleef gespaard. De eigenaar van de woning is vooralsnog onbekend. The post Woning volledig in vlammen opgegaan na overslaande grasbrand appeared first on Suriname Herald .
